A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same HeadHunter and SoftPAG study despite the changed title and extensive reorganization. Their main text, equations, figures, tables and complete appendices are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v3 reports original image-generation experiments, including MS-COCO FID evaluation, preference-score comparisons, and SD3 and FLUX.1 head-selection and stylization results.

after.justification: v4 retains original quantitative and qualitative experiments, including Tables 1–2, general-quality evaluation, style-oriented guidance and appendix head analyses.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1 retains the same iterative generation, scoring and top-k head-selection procedure. SoftPAG and the appendix uniform, mean-query SEG and maximum-attention interpolation variants are unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions retain MS-COCO evaluation, general-quality and style-oriented generation, unseen-content testing, and content-only/null-prompt scenarios. The latter analyses move to Appendix D in v4; trimming illustrative examples does not change the retained task coverage.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains the unguided baseline, CFG at scales 3.0 and 6.0, and CFG combined with HeadHunter. Table 2 retains Uniform Matrix, Query Mean and Identity Matrix comparisons. The head-versus-layer comparisons use the same methods.

E3.justification: The stated protocols match, including 20 search prompt-seed pairs, 1K MS-COCO evaluation prompts, 50 unseen content prompts, search rounds, sampling steps, guidance scales and interpolation grids. Reduced figure panels do not establish a changed experimental protocol.

E4.justification: Figure 2 drops the L3 and L8 examples supporting the head-versus-layer analysis, retaining L12 and L13. The interpolation sensitivity, head-distribution, prompt-dependence and weak-head composition analyses remain, often relocated to appendices.

E5.justification: The prompt-seed lists in Tables 3–4 and averaging procedures are unchanged. Neither version adds repeated-run uncertainty estimates, confidence intervals or formal significance tests.

E6.justification: Figure 2 removes the L3/L8 qualitative results, and Figure 7 reduces each style comparison from three content examples to two. Retained samples are reused. Tables 1–2 and the numerical plots report unchanged values and trends.

T1.justification: The head-level formulation, interpolation and temperature-limit definitions, and search-cost expression are unchanged. Background equations are condensed: diffusion/flow equations become inline, and SEG query blurring remains described in Appendix C.2 despite losing its separate preliminary equation. No substantive mathematical revision appears.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions and conclusion retain the same claims about head specialization, compositional control, HeadHunter and SoftPAG. The broader title does not introduce a new scientific contribution or stronger performance claim.

C2.justification: Section 4.1.1 drops v3's explanation that one search round suffices because structural realism dominates human preference. Interpretations concerning compositionality, prompt-dependent styles, artifact control and computational limitations remain, including material moved into appendices.

D1.justification: v4 omits the direct SD3-Medium checkpoint link supplied in v3's preliminaries. Model identification, the project link, FLUX checkpoint citation, hyperparameters, prompt-seed lists, hardware and approximately three-hour search-cost disclosure remain.

R1.justification: v4 removes the detailed positioning against reward-based fine-tuning, noise optimization and sample-level guidance, dropping associated citations such as DPOK, ReNO and Sampling Demons, alongside several background references. The central positioning against layer-level perturbation guidance remains.

P1.justification: v4 substantially condenses the preliminaries and preference-alignment discussion, moves substantial head-analysis and interpolation material into reorganized appendices, and adds a contents list and funding acknowledgments. The title and several headings also change.

P2.justification: Figures 1, 2 and 7 are compressed or rearranged. Figure 8 is redrawn around one existing case while the full earlier display remains as Figure 21. Numerous analytical figures move into appendices, with extensive resizing and page reflow beyond simple renumbering.

improvement.justification: v4's condensed preliminaries and organized appendix contents improve focus and navigation while preserving the methods and quantitative evidence. Fewer qualitative examples and the loss of some contextual discussion and a checkpoint link modestly reduce completeness, limiting the overall gain to a presentation improvement.
